title_as_printed: Self-evaluation mobile application on mild cognitive impairment based on MiniMental State Examination with bilingual support

blind_codes.Sample_N: Not reported for the user survey; focus group n=8 (plus an unstated number of nursing experts)

Task_Type.reason: Describes the design of an app with an informal usability evaluation; no discrimination figure.

Category.reason: The primary domain is a digital, smartphone-delivered test with speech, gesture, drawing and GPS input (C4), which the registry codes. The test content is the MMSE, a neuropsychological screen (C5); the registry omits that secondary domain.
Category.quote: Our application provides MMSE question sets in both English and Cantonese, two languages commonly used in Hong Kong. Artificial intelligence technologies are applied in the application to enhance user-friendliness and accuracy of verbal and gesture input.

Sample_N_Approx.reason: The only participant number printed is the eight-person focus group. The larger user survey has no reported N, so the true total is unknown. '8 (focus group)' is a supported figure for one component; 'Not reported' would also be defensible.
Sample_N_Approx.quote: Eight smartphone users were further invited to participate in a focus group interview.

notes: The source is a book chapter (Chapter 9 of 'Artificial Intelligence and Big Data Analytics for Smart Healthcare', Elsevier 2021), not a journal research article. Its evaluation is informal: users were 'randomly invited' with no N reported, and neither MCI status nor screening accuracy was assessed. This bears on whether it should count as an included empirical study in the census denominators.
